summary: Padlock Hill's 1940 CCC-built steel tower, moved to the NY State Fairgrounds in the early 1980s and now part of a DEC exhibit; sources disagree on its height.

facts.design: Steel tower with a glass-enclosed cab; newspaper items give 75 feet (1940) and 68 feet (1941)

access.note: Displayed as part of a permanent DEC exhibit at the New York State Fairgrounds. The sources read do not say whether the cab can be entered.

events.note: CCC enrollees from Camp SP-125 at Slaterville built the steel tower on Blackman Hill in the Town of Caroline. A 1940 Ithaca Journal item gives 75 feet.
Russell J. Boyer of Slaterville Springs was appointed observer for the spring fire season, when the tower went into operation. A 1941 item gives 68 feet.
Removed to the State Fairgrounds in the early 1980s (no exact year given). It became part of a DEC exhibit, now described as permanent.

evidence.supports: 1940: site chosen on Blackman Hill in the Town of Caroline by the Conservation Department
evidence.quote: Blackman Hill in the Town of Caroline, one of the highest central points in Tompkins County, was the site chosen by the New York State Conservation Department for the erection of a fire observation tower

evidence.supports: Ten CCC boys from Camp SP-125 worked about two months on the tower
evidence.quote: Ten CCC boys from Camp SP-125 at Slaterville, under the direction of Kenneth G. VanNostrand, camp construction foreman, have been working for two months on the tower

evidence.supports: tower erected at Padlock Hill in 1940
evidence.quote: In 1940, a tower was erected at Padlock Hill

evidence.supports: 1940 item: 75 feet high, 17 feet square at base, 7 feet at top
evidence.quote: the tower measures 17 feet square at the bottom and narrows down to 7 feet square at the top, and is 75 feet high.

evidence.supports: 1940 Ithaca Journal article titled Caroline Fire Tower nears Completion
1941 item: the first fire tower in this section has just been put in operation
evidence.quote: The first fire tower erected in this section has just been put in operation.

evidence.supports: 1941 item: the tower, known as the Padlock Fire Tower, is in the Town of Caroline
evidence.quote: The tower, known as the Padlock Fire Tower, is located in the Town of Caroline, on Blackman Hill, at an elevation of 1,920 feet.

evidence.supports: 1941 item: 68 feet high, erected last year by Slaterville Springs CCC enrollees
evidence.quote: It is 68 feet high and was erected last year by enrollees of Slaterville Springs CCC Camp under supervision of F.E. Fohrman, superintendent.

evidence.supports: Russell J. Boyer appointed observer for the spring fire season
evidence.quote: Russell J. Boyer of Slaterville Springs has been appointed observer and will be on duty daily during the spring fire season.

evidence.supports: fires reported to the CCC camp, whose enrollees would put out fires on state reforestation land
evidence.quote: Fires detected from this tower will be reported to the CCC Camp at Slaterville Springs, and all fires occurring on or near state-owned reforestation areas will be extinguished by the enrollees from this camp.

evidence.supports: steel tower with a glass-enclosed cab on top
evidence.quote: It is of steel with stairway from base to glass enclosed cabin on top.

evidence.supports: removed to the State Fairgrounds in the early 1980s and made part of a DEC exhibit
evidence.quote: Early 1980's: The tower was removed to the State Fairgrounds, where it became a part of the Department of Environmental Conservation exhibit.

evidence.supports: now part of the permanent DEC exhibit at the NY State Fairgrounds
evidence.quote: Padlock Fire Tower is now a part of the permanent DEC exhibit at the New York State Fairgrounds.

evidence.supports: previously stood on Blackman Hill in Potato Hill State Forest
evidence.quote: Previously, the tower stood on Blackman Hill in Potato Hill State Forest 12 miles southeast of Ithaca.

evidence.supports: 2025 newsletter dates the Padlock Hill tower to 1940
evidence.quote: In 1940, a tower was erected at Padlock Hill and in 1941 at Morgan Hill

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1940 Ithaca Journal article was headlined Caroline Fire Tower; the 1941 item and the DEC use Padlock Fire Tower. The story uses Padlock and notes the earlier headline.

notes_for_editor: Heights conflict: 75 feet in the August 1940 Ithaca Journal item, 68 feet in the April 1941 item. No height is recorded in facts for that reason. The early-1980s move has no exact year in the sources read, so the relocated event has no year key. The record's status 'standing' fits: the tower is on display at the fairgrounds. Whether the cab can be entered is unknown. No fires are named in the sources read. No photos added (no image URLs were read). The Forest Lookouts page transcribes Ithaca Journal items, so those quotes are secondhand transcriptions.
